concepts.title: Characteristics of Living Beings
concepts.definition: Living beings grow, breathe, take in food, respond to their surroundings, excrete waste and reproduce; a shell that seems still may hold a snail busy doing all of these.
concepts.formula: life = growth + respiration + nutrition + response + excretion + reproduction
concepts.key_idea: Life is a bundle of processes: any creature showing them, even inside a shell, is alive.
question_patterns: list the characteristics of living beings
how do living things respond to their surroundings
why is growth a sign of life
what is respiration in simple words
why do living beings excrete
is a snail inside its shell living how do we know

concepts.title: Germination of a Seed
concepts.definition: A seed looks lifeless, yet given air, water and warmth it wakes: the root pushes down, the shoot rises, and germination turns a stored little plant into a growing one.
concepts.key_idea: A seed is life waiting for conditions: supply the three needs and growth begins at once.
question_patterns: what conditions does a seed need to germinate
what comes out first from a germinating seed
why does a seed fail to sprout without water
design an activity to study germination
where is the food stored in a seed
why is warmth needed for germination

Give the overall picture in one sentence.

concepts.title: Life Cycles of Plants and Animals
concepts.definition: Living beings pass through stages: a seed becomes a seedling, a plant, then flowers and seeds again; insects hatch, grow, transform and lay eggs, each life cycle turning in its own rhythm.
concepts.key_idea: Life repeats itself in stages: every cycle links one generation to the next without a break.
question_patterns: draw the life cycle of a plant
describe the stages in the life cycle of a butterfly
how does the life cycle of a plant begin and end
which stage of an insect's life differs most from the adult
compare the life cycles of a plant and a frog
what would happen if living beings did not reproduce

concepts.title: Living and Non-living: The Puzzle
concepts.definition: A car moves but does not grow or reproduce; a cloud grows but does not breathe or respond; the puzzle of the chapter is settled by checking the full list of life processes, not any single one.
concepts.key_idea: One sign is not enough: life is declared only when the whole set of processes holds.
